segments: [Pekah] of Israel brought Rezin, king of Syria,
and went up against Judah,
and slaughtered one hundred and twenty thousand.
Ahaz, however, the king of Jerusalem, sent to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria,
and he came and killed Rezin,
and waged war against Damascus,
and took the Edomites (the Arameans?) captive,
and took much silver from them,
and departed to his country.
And in the second year of Ahaz, Hoshea rebelled against Pekah and killed him,
and reigned over Israel nine years.
And in the eighth year of Ahaz,
Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, went up against Israel,
and Hoshea became subject to him,
and gave him tribute.
And afterwards he rebelled,
and sent to Adrammelech the Ethiopian, who was dwelling in Egypt, to come to his aid.
And when Shalmaneser heard,
he went up again against Samaria,
and encamped against it for three years,
and conquered it, and exiled the children of Israel to Babylon—the ten tribes.
For this was the first captivity.
Now from Adam until this year, which is the eleventh year of Ahaz,
was four thousand seven hundred and thirty [years].
Now Ahaz took down the Sea of bronze from the bronze oxen,
which Solomon had made.
At this time the island of Rhodes was built,
and it lasted one thousand four hundred and five years,
until the foreigners {OCR?} uprooted it.
And there were also built in Sicily the city of Selinus and Segesta {OCR?},
and in Pontus, Trebizond,
and in Bithynia, Cyzicus,
and in Italy, Croton and Lucania.
And in the seventh year of Ahaz, Romulus became king,
and built in Italy Rome, that great and renowned [city],
and dwelt in it. For until this [time] the kings of Italy were called Latins,
and from here on, Romans, that is, Franks.
After Ahaz,
Hezekiah his son [reigned] twenty-nine years.
While the land of Samaria and the whole dominion of the Israelites were subjugated by the Assyrians,
Hezekiah alone remained reigning over Judah in Jerusalem.
And in the eighth year of Hezekiah, Shalmaneser the Assyrian sent men to guard the land of Judah.
And because the Lord sent lions upon them,
Shalmaneser commanded that they keep the law of the God of the land.
And he sent them a certain priest named Azariah to teach them the Law of Moses;
and he wrote for them the Torah in Hebrew.
